messages:
maria: quick sync re: safetensors warmup instability. I sketched a lightweight sidecar + lease approach that trades a tiny amount of metadata for safer streaming and faster hotpatches. looking for pushback before i file the RFC.

ben: short version? we already debated canonical-sidecar vs index-first last week.

maria: new bits: (1) explicit commit token file (.commit) written after sidecar so loaders can avoid torn views on eventual-consistent stores; (2) allow a "lazy-validate" fast-path where we do minimal header checks + per-shard lazy checksum; (3) explicit sidecar TTL/lease so aborted uploads don't leave stale commits.

rachel: commit file helps with S3 visibility races, nice. How does loader decide to use fast-path vs safe full-parse?

maria: policy idea: loader GETs sidecar.commit (very small). If present and lease active -> GET sidecar.json and check header_prefix (first 24 bytes of sha256 base64url). If header_prefix matches quick-range digest we proceed to stream shards but verify each shard checksum when fetched. Background task completes full header validation and emits metrics.

ben: so we accept a short window where header might be wrong but per-shard checks protect correctness. How costly are those per-shard checks for typical cold-start flows?

maria: we only verify shards on-demand, not eagerly for entire bundle. For short prompts cold-start might only touch a few shards; overhead limited. Metric to measure: avg_extra_range_bytes and cold_start_p50/p95.

kyle: what about hotpatch (delta) application? we want apply-small-patch without rewriting whole bundle.

maria: sidecar includes optional delta_manifest referencing canonical_shard_ids and patch_ops. Publisher must include delta_base_digest in commit. Loader will only apply patch if current canonical digest equals delta_base_digest. Patch application is a seq of shard-range fetches + atomic swap of in-memory routing table; no file-system rename needed on serving side.

rachel: atomicity on ingest side? how do we avoid seeing sidecar with commit but missing shard objects?

maria: ingest flow: write objects -> write sidecar.tmp -> fsync-equivalent -> obtain lease token from control plane -> write sidecar.commit containing lease + header_digest and fsync -> rename tmp -> final name. Loaders treat presence of sidecar.commit as the committed signal. If rename fails, lease expires and commit is rejected by loaders.

ben: edge case: cross-region read where commit appears but lease validation call to control plane fails due to network partition. Loader shouldn't block the request for long.

maria: loader behavior: if lease-check RPC times out, loader can optionally consult an exponential backoff + local heuristic: fetch small header ranges and compare against registry-stored canonical digest (if we have it cached). If match, allow fast-path but emit metric lease_validation_timeout and apply conservative per-shard verification. Default enterprise policy: require lease check; public customers can opt into heuristic earlier.

kyle: CI and tests? we need harness that simulates partial uploads, commit races, and delta patches.

ci-bot: build 5028 queued for branch feat/sidecar-lease-tests. integration-suite will run churn + eventual-consistency scenarios.

rachel: another operational concern: sidecar GETs add metadata ops. For very high QPS cold-starts we might overwhelm metadata tier. Proposal: cache sidecar in CDN/edge for hot model variants and use a short TTL config. Also instrument sidecar_cache_hit and sidecar_get_latency.

maria: agreed. sidecar size target: < 4KB if possible. Schema minimal fields: version, header_digest_prefix, canonical_version, shards: [{id, offset, len, checksum_b64}], optional delta_manifest, encoding. Keep it compact so caching is effective.

ben: fallback story for old bundles? loader should detect absence of sidecar.commit and fall back to legacy full-header parse and previous warmup paths. Back-compat is important.

maria: exactly. Loader state machine: 1) commit present & lease ok -> fast-path with lazy-validate; 2) commit present & lease unknown -> optional heuristic or blocked depending on tenant; 3) commit absent -> legacy full-parse.

kyle: what failure modes should trigger immediate rollback/fallback during request? If a shard checksum fails mid-stream we should abort request and switch to fallback model or failover node. Also increment metric shard_validation_failure and emit debug bundle id for postmortem.

rachel: add audit logs for commit writes + lease ids so support can debug hotpatch miswrites. Also include clear error codes: 412 commit_missing, 428 lease_mismatch, 422 checksum_fail, 504 lease_rpc_timeout.

maria: good list. i'll include those in RFC. next steps: i'll open RFC PR with sidecar schema + ingest pseudo-code + loader state machine + test plan. ben/hk/kyle can stub loader changes behind feature flag; rachel will add integration tests in harness for eventual consistency + delta patches.

ci-bot: integration job 5028 started. results will be posted.

maria: thanks all. filing RFC tomorrow unless anyone objects. reopen thread if anything else pops up.
